desc: Ideation/invariants: monotone non-expansive map, no splitting after merge, count(B)≤count(A) necessary, cut-flow view; naive assignment-bottleneck formula wrong.
Brute-force BFS ground truth for N≤7 (multiset states via combinations_with_replacement after crash fix) + assignment-bottleneck candidate DP.
Scheduling model insight: H3 "boundary room" hypothesis refuted — {1,4,5}→{2,4,5} solvable in 2 at N=5,6,7; boundary never affects answers.

Exact per-partition model derived: D_t = d_t − d_{t+1} ≥ 0 (contraction), parity chain β_{t+1} = β_1 ⊕ (D_t mod 2) feasible iff β_t+β_{t+1} ≤ D_t, M = (S+β_1+β_m)/2, k = |d_1 − M + β_1| + M; correction ∈ {0,1}; parity failures only at zero-reduction cuts; hand-verified on samples and all key cases.

Efficient algorithm design: K, S, d_1, d_m and β_m = β_1 ⊕ (S mod 2) all partition-independent ⇒ closed-form k(β_1) for β_1 ∈ {0,1}; feasibility per β_1 reduces to greedy increasing cut selection with per-cut allowed sets (g_s ≥ h_j; zero-reduction cuts need (p_s − q_j) ≡ (β_1+d_1) mod 2); O(N) per test case.

Final O(N) solution implemented with fast byte-level I/O (buffer.read().split(), handles T≤2e5, sum N≤1e6), plus flag-guarded self-test comparing against BFS ground truth over all N≤7 pairs (~21k), the three samples (3,-1,5), and ten named edge cases (A==B, r>m, m=1, r=m, adjacent merges, parity obstruction 101101→101010→-1, 10011→01011→2). All cases hand-traced to match; self-test is self-reporting (`OVERALL: ALL TESTS PASSED`).
